newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Sidek Q3 results seen debt-ridden.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sidek Q3 results seen debt-ridden.

text.p: Holding company Grupo Sidek's debt restructuring plan will be crucial to its third quarter earnings which analysts expect to be poor.

"We don't know what the final outcome (of the debt restructuring plan) will be, we don't know what shape the company will take," said Bond Snodgrass, analyst at the Abaco brokerage in Mexico City, "they have to solve these two unknowns."
Another analyst, who declined to be named, said Sidek's delay in settling on a debt restructuring plan had turned investors away.
"There's very little interest," the analyst said, "(investors) are just not interested in the losses they have been making since 1995."
Analysts did not expect earnings to be attractive, either. "Operating earnings for the third quarter will be very poor, said Santiago Pique, analyst at Bear Stearns in New York.
"We do not expect any great changes," Snodgrass said.
Another analyst did expect losses per share to fall.
Victor Ortiz from the Bursametric brokerage estimated earnings per share at negative 3.7 pesos for the third quarter, compared to negative 4.19 pesos for the first half of 1996.
Ortiz said he expected the relative improvement "due to a slight improvement in non-cash items" and said that the "market is improving for its tourist arm, Situr."
Sidek has had considerable financial trouble since the peso devaluation crisis in December 1994, due to its heavy indebtedness in dollars and a fall in revenues.

Sidek incurred a foreign exchange loss of $58.3 million dollars in January 1995, and postponed a foreign debt payment of $19.5 million for one day in February 1995, which led to jitters in the Mexican Stock Market.
Sidek was bailed out by 17 Mexican banks, but low domestic revenues have failed to offset its heavy indebtedness in dollars.
Sidek's period of grace with debtor banks expires in November, when it is due to present a debt restructuring plan.
Press reports said that Sidek owed Mexican banks a total of 11.416 billion pesos at the end of the first half of 1996, which was an estimated 73 percent of the company's total debt.
Sidek is a holding company for tourist subsidiary Situr, steelmaking firm Simec, shipbuilding arm Sinam, housing developers Siturbe and factoring firm Kapital House.
